text_blocks.snippet: In Virginia, a religious exemption from school vaccination requirements can be obtained by completing and notarizing the Commonwealth of Virginia Certificate of Religious Exemption (Form CRE 1). This form must be submitted to the school, and it affirms that the administration of vaccines conflicts with the student's religious beliefs.
snippet_highlighted_words: completing and notarizing the Commonwealth of Virginia Certificate of Religious Exemption (Form CRE 1)

list.title: 1. Obtain the Form:
list.snippet: The Certificate of Religious Exemption (Form CRE 1) can be obtained from the Virginia Department of Health or the Home Educators Association of Virginia.

list.title: 2. Complete the Form:
list.snippet: Fill out the form accurately, providing the student's information and detailing how the religious beliefs conflict with vaccination.

list.title: 3. Notarize the Form:
list.snippet: Have the completed form notarized by a qualified notary public.

list.title: 4. Submit to the School:
list.snippet: Submit the notarized Certificate of Religious Exemption to the student's school.

list.title: 5. Maintain a Copy:
list.snippet: It's recommended to keep a copy of the completed and notarized form for your records.

list.title: Not a General Exemption:
list.snippet: A religious exemption from vaccinations does not extend to other school-related requirements, such as compulsory attendance.

list.title: Employer Responsibilities:
list.snippet: Employers in Virginia may also have policies regarding religious exemptions for vaccination requirements, and they may have their own procedures for reviewing requests.

list.title: Reasonable Accommodation:
list.snippet: Employers may need to provide reasonable accommodations for employees with religious exemptions, but they can also determine the validity of the sincerely held belief.
